key_insight: MRI-derived kidney geometry combined with FEM elastography produced biomechanical features that distinguished CKD from healthy controls.
engineering_relevance: The framework could support renal biomechanical assessment from conventional MRI without dedicated magnetic resonance elastography acquisition.
method: Convert kidney segmentation masks into watertight surfaces and tetrahedral FEM meshes.
Simulate harmonic waves using a nearly incompressible Kelvin–Voigt tissue model, then estimate complex shear modulus via Helmholtz inversion.
Classify CKD using machine learning trained on FEM-derived biomechanical features.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stiffness estimates consistent with published human renal MRE ranges and classification performance up to 86.26% cross-validation accuracy with an AUC of 0.92.
watch_item: Independent patient-specific stiffness validation is not reported in the abstract, so agreement with published ranges does not establish measurement accuracy.
paper_title: Finite Element Elastographic Analysis of Kidney MRI for Computational Assessment of Chronic Kidney Disease
